description: Excessive alcohol can potentiate metformin's effect on lactate metabolism and is a risk factor for metformin-associated lactic acidosis.

Aluminium-containing antacids can reduce fexofenadine absorption; separate administration by at least 2 hours.
Aluminium-containing antacids reduce levofloxacin absorption when taken within 2 hours; separate doses by at least 2 hours.
Amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure; the simvastatin dose should not exceed 20 mg daily when used together.

Ibuprofen can interfere with the antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin and the combination may increase adverse effects. Timing matters; ask a clinician or pharmacist about an alternative or schedule.
Using aspirin with warfarin increases bleeding risk because of their combined effects on hemostasis. Monitor for bleeding and seek clinician guidance.

Atenolol may mask tachycardia, a warning sign of hypoglycemia, although at recommended doses it does not potentiate insulin-induced hypoglycemia or delay glucose recovery. Monitor glucose and symptoms.
Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and can raise atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk. Dose limitation and clinical monitoring may be needed.
Itraconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and can raise atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk. Dose limitation and clinical monitoring may be needed.
Azithromycin may increase coagulation time with warfarin; monitor prothrombin time/INR during concurrent use.
Calcium can reduce doxycycline absorption; separate calcium and doxycycline doses according to the product label or pharmacist's advice.
Calcium carbonate can bind levothyroxine and reduce absorption. Separate doses by at least 4 hours.
Cetirizine can add to clonazepam-related drowsiness and impaired alertness. Avoid driving or other risky tasks if affected.
Ciprofloxacin with sulfonylureas including glimepiride has been associated with sometimes severe hypoglycemia; monitor blood glucose closely.
Magnesium-containing antacids reduce ciprofloxacin absorption. Separate ciprofloxacin by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after the antacid.
Ciprofloxacin can enhance warfarin anticoagulation; monitor INR and signs of bleeding during concomitant use.
Clarithromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4; avoid the combination because simvastatin concentrations and rhabdomyolysis risk can rise markedly.
Levocetirizine may add to clonazepam-related drowsiness and impaired alertness. Avoid driving or other risky tasks if affected.

Clopidogrel with an NSAID increases gastrointestinal bleeding risk. Use only with clinician guidance and monitor for bleeding.

Avoid this combination: omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and significantly reduces clopidogrel's antiplatelet activity, even when doses are separated by 12 hours.

Iodinated contrast imaging can require temporary metformin interruption in specified patients because of renal impairment and lactic-acidosis risk. Follow the imaging team's instructions and restart only when advised.
Cyclosporine markedly increases rosuvastatin exposure and myopathy risk; use only with strict prescriber dose limits and monitoring.
NSAIDs can reduce renal lithium clearance and raise serum lithium concentrations; check lithium levels and toxicity symptoms when combined.
NSAIDs may reduce losartan's blood-pressure effect and, especially in older, volume-depleted, or renally impaired patients, worsen renal function. Monitor blood pressure and renal function.
NSAIDs may attenuate telmisartan's blood-pressure effect and increase renal impairment risk, particularly with renal impairment, volume depletion, or diuretic use.
Iron can reduce doxycycline absorption; separate iron and doxycycline doses according to the product label or pharmacist's advice.
An SSRI with an NSAID can increase bleeding risk; monitor for gastrointestinal or other bleeding and ask a clinician before regular combined use.
SSRIs including escitalopram can increase bleeding risk with warfarin; monitor for bleeding and ensure the prescriber knows about the combination.
Fluconazole inhibits glimepiride metabolism and can increase glimepiride exposure and hypoglycemia risk; monitor blood glucose closely.
Fluconazole can increase phenytoin exposure; monitor phenytoin concentrations and toxicity during coadministration.
Corticosteroids can worsen glucose control and reduce the glucose-lowering effect of sulfonylureas; monitor glucose closely.
Hydrochlorothiazide reduces renal lithium clearance and can greatly increase lithium toxicity risk; this combination generally should be avoided or managed with close monitoring by the prescriber.

NSAIDs may attenuate telmisartan's blood-pressure effect and increase renal impairment risk, particularly with renal impairment, volume depletion, or diuretic use.
Ibuprofen with warfarin increases bleeding risk through independent effects. Avoid unless specifically directed and monitor for bleeding.
Systemic corticosteroids such as prednisolone can raise blood glucose and may require closer glucose monitoring or adjustment of diabetes treatment by the prescriber.
Sitagliptin used with insulin increases hypoglycemia risk; the insulin dose may need adjustment by the prescriber.

Levofloxacin has been associated with increased INR and bleeding when used with warfarin; monitor INR and signs of bleeding.
Losartan and other angiotensin receptor blockers have been associated with increased serum lithium and toxicity; monitor lithium concentrations closely.

Repeated regular paracetamol use may increase INR in some patients taking warfarin. Check INR when starting or stopping repeated use; occasional use may differ.
Rosuvastatin may increase INR in patients receiving warfarin. Monitor INR when rosuvastatin is initiated, discontinued, or dose-adjusted.
